routes.description: Establish that the earliest Christian evidence and subsequent corroborating traditions are best explained by an earthly Jewish man whose execution, relatives, and followers preceded resurrection belief.
routes.successCriteria: Connect Pauline bodily, genealogical, and familial language to ordinary human existence, then support that reading with sufficiently independent narrative, non-Christian, or remembered relational evidence.

motionBridge.description: Show that early Christian belief presupposed a recently living earthly Jesus rather than originating solely with a celestial or mythic figure.

centralBridges.description: Establish that Paul's birth, ancestry, death, burial, and crucifixion language refers to events involving an earthly Jewish person.
Establish that Paul's designation of James identifies a biological relative and therefore an early personal link to Jesus's human family.
Establish that narrative, Roman, Jewish, or early Christian sources provide materially independent corroboration of Jesus, his execution, or his relatives.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain how early conversion, witness, and resurrection traditions fit belief centered on a recently executed person.
Show that Jewish Davidic and messianic expectations make ordinary earthly descent and public execution contextually intelligible.

routes.description: Establish that the earliest evidence remains compatible with a celestial Christ derived from scripture and revelation, while later earthly narratives and corroborating claims lack demonstrable independence.
routes.successCriteria: Provide coherent celestial readings of the principal Pauline data and show that later sources, familial claims, and appearance traditions do not supply reliable independent evidence requiring a historical founder.

motionBridge.description: Show that early Christian belief can originate with a celestial or mythic Christ without requiring a historical Jesus later remembered in narrative.

centralBridges.description: Show that Paul's language about embodiment, ancestry, death, burial, and revelation remains compatible with a celestial incarnation and drama.
Show that brother-of-the-Lord language and its surrounding grammar do not establish a biological relationship between James and Jesus.
Show that the Gospels, Acts, and later historical references are late, dependent, unsourced, or otherwise unable to provide independent corroboration.
Explain Christianity's origins through comparable mythic patterns, revelatory experiences, and later historicizing narrative development.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Apply source loss, arguments from silence, and comparative likelihoods consistently when determining what the surviving record should contain.
Account for resurrection and group-appearance traditions through ecstatic or revelatory experiences without presupposing encounters with a revived earthly person.

sections.title: Pauline embodiment, birth, ancestry, death, and burial
sections.rationale: The earliest writings are the principal common evidentiary ground, and their language must distinguish ordinary earthly biography from a materially embodied but celestial incarnation and death.

sections.title: James and the meaning of brother of the Lord
sections.rationale: Whether Paul identifies a biological relative provides a direct early test of Jesus's human family, while grammar, naming conventions, and fictive kinship determine the force of that identification.

sections.title: Independence and reliability of later corroboration
sections.rationale: The Gospels, Luke-Acts, Tacitus, Josephus, Hegesippus, and related traditions matter insofar as they preserve information independent of Christian narrative development or later informants.

sections.title: Resurrection appearances, conversion, and early movement origins
sections.rationale: Paul's conversion, persecution, and reported appearances bear on whether the movement began around a recently executed person or around revelatory experiences subsequently interpreted and narrated.

sections.title: Comparative mythic models and documentary expectations
sections.rationale: Comparisons with historicized savior figures, expected documentary traces, and arguments from silence frame how strongly the surviving evidence differentiates the competing origin accounts.
